**In this chapter:** scripts, comments, objects, functions and vectors.

## Use a script

Code typed in the Console is gone when you close RStudio. Code in a script is saved.

File > New File > R Script. Save it in your project as `practice.R`. Run a line by putting the cursor on it and pressing **Ctrl+Enter** (Windows) or **Cmd+Enter** (Mac).

## Comments

Anything after `#` is ignored by R. Use comments to say what your code does.

```{r}
# R can be used as a calculator
2 + 3
```

## Objects

Store a value with `<-` and give it a name. Typing the name shows the value.

```{r}
height <- 172
height
```

Names are case-sensitive: `Height` and `height` are different objects.

## Functions

A function does a job. You give it **arguments** inside brackets, separated by commas.

```{r}
round(3.14159, digits = 2)
```

Here `round` is the function, and `3.14159` and `digits = 2` are its arguments. To see a function's arguments, open its help page:

```{r}
#| eval: false
?round
```

## Vectors

A vector is a set of values. Make one with `c()` (short for combine).

```{r}
heights <- c(165, 172, 180, 158)
mean(heights)
length(heights)
```

Most functions work on the whole vector at once:

```{r}
heights / 100
```

## Your turn

Make a vector of the ages of five people you know. Use `mean()`, `min()` and `max()` on it. Add a comment above each line saying what it does.
